sophia: FYI ran CI evals + perf runs for opt-6.7b after yesterday's kernel-selector change — seeing ~20% throughput drop and a small correctness delta (2-3 token mismatches) on activation-quant paths. Repro locally with perf harness.

raj: ouch. any smoke logs or profiler output?

sophia: pasted quick profiler snippet below, trimmed:
```
-- timeline (ms) --
quantize: 12.1
pack-kv: 1.8
fp8-gemm(kernel A): 6.2
kernel-switch(overhead): 4.9
copy-kv: 3.1
batching-wait: 9.4
-- total per step ~37.5 (prev ~30) --
```
Looks like repeated kernel-switch + batching-wait spikes when serving pinned sequences with large KV cache.

david: does kernel-selector now prefer fp8-gemm for short sequences? we added a heuristic to switch kernels based on avg-seq-len, might be thrashing with small batches.

sophia: yes selector picks fp8 for most layers. but the weird bit is correctness delta — tokens differ only when KV hits cross a segment boundary.

tanya: could be scaling state carried over in KV blocks. FP8 activation needs per-chunk scale/zero-point; if KV packing reuses a buffer but scale metadata isn't updated -> silent corruption.

raj: that matches a repro I had last week where layering a batching change + kv-compact caused stale metadata reads. can you share a minimal repro?

sophia: repro steps condensed:
1) run model with mixprec fp16->fp8 activation saving kv to shared pool (simulate dedup)
2) enable aggressive batching (batch_timeout 5ms) so some requests share kernels but different seq-lens
3) run eval prompt set A -> see token drift after ~2000 steps

sophia: quick log with patch-level prints:
```
[layer 8] chosen kernel: fp8-gemm, activation_scale: 3.2e-2
[kv read] block_id=42, scale_meta=3.2e-2
[layer 9] chosen kernel: fp8-gemm, activation_scale: 2.9e-2  <-- recomputed
[matmul] using scale meta 3.2e-2 (mismatch) -> tiny numeric diff
```

david: that is a smoking gun. packing/unpacking path must update scale_meta atomically with new kv block. if we race packing + kernel selection the matmul will read the old scale.

tanya: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) pin kernel selector to fp16 for opt-6.7b on the canary until we fix, 2) in the kv packer, add a version token that matmul validates before using scale_meta (cheap guard).

raj: also consider delaying kernel-switch until batch boundary commit. the extra kernel-switch cost is costly and increases window for stale-state races. can we keep kernel pinned per-request until its KV is fully applied?

sophia: agreed. patch I'm trying: set per-request kernel_hint, skip selector for active requests, and add transient kv_version check in fp8 path. preliminary runs -> throughput back to ~31.5 (partial recovery) and token diffs gone in 5k steps.

perf-bot: Alert: regression_detected(opt-6.7b-mixprec) severity=medium -> linked ticket RW-3921

david: nice. we should:
- create a deterministic unit test that simulates kv packing + concurrent kernel selection (low-cost fuzz)
- add kv_version assert in fp8 matmul path (opt-in via env for canary)
- schedule canary rollout with kernel pinned to fp16 for 24h after fix

tanya: I'll own the unit test + kv_version guard. raj can you own the rollout policy change?

raj: yep. will add a temporary feature-flag gate and a dashboard to track kernel-switch count + kv_version-mismatch metric.

sophia: thanks team. I'll open the PR for the guard + selector-skip and attach perf traces. cc @david for review.

david: lgtm. small follow-up: we should add lightweight telemetry to record per-layer scale recompute frequency (helps catch calibration thrash from live traffic).

sophia: good call. will add to PR. estimated timeline: hotfix PR today, unit tests + canary tomorrow, full rollout after 48h of canary stability.

raj: sound plan. also note: if we keep selector heuristics too aggressive we risk more kernel warmups on shared hardware — might want a global throttle on kernel_switch/sec per-GPU.

tanya: ack. file notes in RW-3921.

sophia: attaching perf traces + small repro script link: https://redwood.dev/s/frag/opt6-repro (internal).

perf-bot: Ticket RW-3921 updated: status=in_progress, assignees=[tanya, sophia, raj], priority=high

sophia: will update thread with PR link when ready. thanks all :heart:
